newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finland Bank governor says ERM2 is good framework.
newsitem.headline: Finland Bank governor says ERM2 is good framework.

text.p: Economic convergence outside the Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) will be well managed by the planned exchange rate mechanism ERM2, Bank of Finland governor Sirkka Hamalainen said on Tuesday.

"ERM2 is a valuable framework for managing the convergence of the countries outside the single currency area," she said in a prepared speech to the subcommittee on monetary affairs of the European Parliament.
"The countries participating in ERM2 commit themselves to credible converegence programmes that emphasize fiscal consolidation," she said.

She said Finland should be eligible to participate in EMU from the beginning of stage three based on its performance. She also said the stability pact outlined at the Ecofin meeting in September gave a point of departure for efforts to make a demanding but flexible EMU, she said.
Hamalainen added Finland has already coverged with Europe so it has become less vulnerable.

"It can be seen that the increasing convergence of Finland's export structure with that of other EU countries, the diversification of the structure of output in the forest products and metal engineering industries and the changes in economic legislation and policy are promoting convergence with the EU and have already reduced Finland's vulnerability to economic shocks," Hamalainen said.
She said a low inflation performance was ensured in Finland by the moderate wage settlement that reaches until January 1998 and by low inflation expectations.
